findings.reason: the sentence is the plan's stated consequence of the defect and its own cited function contradicts it, so the rationale (and any production check of the fix) names the wrong reader of the delivery.
findings.text: the Why claims "The launch supervisor watches the launched run's own directory (`_supervisor_manifest_path(run_id)`), so it never sees the delivery", but `_supervisor_manifest_path` reads the *recorded* manifest path from the run's live pointer (`_recorded_manifest_path`, `dispatch_sessions.py:926`) and only falls back to the run directory when the pointer names none; for the very instance §22 cites it returns the queued run's path, so the supervisor watches the same file the worker writes and does see the delivery

findings.reason: a builder implementing the sentence as written has to either edit `dispatch.py`/`dispatch_plan.py` (outside the declared write paths) or silently substitute the clear-and-re-derive mechanism, so the plan should state which, since its SPEC is exact.
findings.text: the deliverable places the re-root "when the queued pointer is turned back into a node" and targets "the same relative path under the launched run's directory", but at `_node_from_pointer` the launched run id does not yet exist (it is minted inside `dispatch` via `new_run_id`, and `dispatch()` accepts no `run_id`), while the declared write paths are only `queue_admission.py` and the test; the in-scope implementation is to blank paths under the queued run's directory and let `dispatch_plan.py:477/485` re-derive them
